clue.text: Settle what the not so popular music-hall entertainer must do?

definitions.meaning: to settle a bill is to pay the whole amount owed

definitions.text: what the not so popular music-hall entertainer must do?
definitions.meaning: a weaker act is printed in small type at the bottom of the show's poster

explanation.definitionFit: To pay for everything is to settle up; a lowly act's name sits at the poster's base, its lowest line.

clue.text: Attack against Egyptian deity

parts.note: on can mean against, as in leaning on or against a wall
Set (or Seth) is the Egyptian god of storms and disorder

explanation.surface: Someone takes a stand against an ancient Egyptian god.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is the first rush of an assault, an attack.

clue.text: Nuts are loose in these containers

indicators.note: letters that are loose have come free and can be gathered back in any order

explanation.surface: Some nuts have come loose inside a set of storage jars.
explanation.definitionFit: Large metal vessels with taps for brewing a hot drink are a kind of container.

clue.text: People tangled in her web

indicators.note: something tangled has its strands twisted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Folk caught up in a spider's net woven by a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jewish nation of the Bible are called by this name, so it denotes a people.

clue.text: The elder brother on our family record

parts.note: b. is the genealogists' abbreviation for brother
a family tree records a family's descent

explanation.surface: The eldest sibling is entered on the family's genealogy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The elder' reads as the older brother, but it is the shrub: a Scots name for the elder bush.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Scottish and northern English name for the elder shrub.

clue.text: Someone may be willing to make you his

definitions.text: Someone may be willing to make you his

parts.words: Someone may be willing to make you his
parts.note: willing here means leaving in a will, so you are made the recipient of a bequest

explanation.definitionFit: A person named in a will to receive a bequest is the one a testator makes theirs.

clue.text: Caught inside Berlin, blundering around in a fog

indicators.note: blundering about suggests the letters stumble into a new arrangement

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A spy is trapped in Berlin, stumbling about in thick mist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' looks like a container signal, but its six letters are fodder with C and BERLIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hidden by murk cannot be made out, so it is impossible to perceive.

clue.text: Withdrawn from cast — I'm no use

indicators.note: putting letters to use means working them into a fresh order

explanation.surface: An actor dropped from the cast laments being useless.
explanation.definitionFit: Monastic life is secluded and retired from the world, as withdrawn as a hermit's.

clue.text: NHS timetable's reform causing concern

indicators.note: reforming the letters remakes them into a different shape

parts.note: taken as written, the s included

explanation.surface: A shake-up of hospital schedules in the National Health Service is worrying people.
explanation.walkthrough: NHS is the UK's National Health Service. 'concern' looks like worry but means a business.
explanation.definitionFit: A concern is a business or firm, and an establishment is likewise a business premises or institution.

clue.text: Domestic scene with a girl

parts.note: a nest is a cosy home, the scene of domestic life

explanation.surface: A homely picture of a household with a young woman in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nesta is a Welsh female first name, so it can stand for a girl.

clue.text: An old type, middle-class and conventional

definitions.meaning: a size of printing type, about 9 point

explanation.definitionFit: A traditional printers' size of letter, and an adjective for staid property-owning middle-class values.

clue.text: Cut across and bury the body

parts.note: to inter is to bury in a grave
a sect is a body of followers

explanation.surface: Instructions for an undertaker or a murderer disposing of a corpse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'body' suggests a corpse, which the word 'bury' encourages, but it is a group of believers.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines that cut across each other cross at a point, which is what intersecting means.

clue.text: Crowning feature on top of the temple

definitions.text: Crowning feature on top of the temple

parts.words: Crowning feature on top of the temple
parts.note: the temple is the side of the head, and a jewelled headdress sits above it

explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled ornamental band worn on the head crowns the wearer, sitting above the temples.

clue.text: Very different from chalk!

parts.note: the idiom 'as different as chalk and' a dairy product says two things are utterly unlike

explanation.walkthrough: 'Like chalk and cheese' is a British idiom for two things that are completely different.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom pairs chalk with this dairy food as the classic example of total unlikeness.

clue.text: A draw, then another draw I'd get around this time

indicators.note: tie gets around means its letters enclose the other piece

parts.note: a tie is a drawn game
the D of I'd, its I running into the I of TIE

explanation.surface: Two games end level in a row, and someone talks about coming round at evening.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse needs TIE around ID with the two I's sharing a letter; strictly only the D goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is the evening, the time of day the clue points to.

clue.text: Pet's lead twisted around base of statue

indicators.note: a lead that has got twisted around is knotted into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, the s included

explanation.surface: A dog's lead gets tangled round the plinth of a monument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base of statue' might be read as the last letter of statue, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestal is the block or plinth a statue stands on.

clue.text: In rain storm shape appears frog-like

indicators.note: a storm whips the letters about into a different order

explanation.surface: In a rainstorm, a creature appears that looks like a frog.
explanation.definitionFit: Raniform comes from Latin rana, a frog, and means shaped like one.

clue.text: Start aborted — holding ring he first put inside this device

indicators.note: the shuffled letters hold the other pieces inside them
a start that is aborted is broken up, so the letters come out in a new order
he is put before the ring piece

parts.note: a ring looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A false start with someone fumbling to fit a ring into a gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aborted' scrambles the first word to RSTAT; 'holding' opens it after the R, and 'first' fixes the order of the two inserted pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A rheostat is a variable resistor used to control current, a piece of electrical equipment.

clue.text: A woman's knitted vest suits this painter

definitions.meaning: a woman's knitted undergarment worn over the vest
Stanley ... was an English painter, of Cookham

explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting knitted under-bodice for women, and the surname of the twentieth-century English artist Sir Stanley.

clue.text: Star-fish?

parts.note: not the sea creature but the fishes made of stars, a constellation and zodiac sign

explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac constellation the Fishes is literally fish in the stars.

clue.text: Living with friend,! admitted, can be hip

parts.note: is means exists or is living

indicators.note: the friend lets the other letter in

explanation.surface: Moving in with a pal, once confessed, can be quite fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hip' looks like trendy, but it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The ischium is the lowest bone of the hip, on which a person sits.

clue.text: Inventor's nose I'd put out of joint

indicators.note: something put out of joint is dislocated, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An inventor complains his nose has been put out of joint.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Inventor is 'is', joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Alva, the American who devised the phonograph and electric lamp, is the classic inventor.

clue.text: Twist leaves: take out this fibre

indicators.note: the letters can be taken out of the words where they sit in sequence

explanation.surface: Instructions for twisting and removing the leaves of a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twist' looks like an anagram signal, but the answer runs on through the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Istle is a stiff fibre from Mexican agave and yucca leaves, used for cord and brushes.

clue.text: Bad taste of lemon curd pie began -—- then left off

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Bad taste of lemon curd pie began -—- then left off': the dash is garbled OCR and no letter source for the I is visible, so the I (anagram of LEMON CURD + I less L) cannot be honestly placed
annotationWithheld.clue: Bad taste of lemon curd pie began -—- then left off

clue.text: File on English author

indicators.note: in a down clue the file sits on top of the other letter

parts.note: a rasp is a coarse file

explanation.surface: A dossier on an English writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Rudolf Erich Raspe wrote the Baron Munchausen tales, first published in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Raspe was the German writer of the Munchausen stories, so he is an author.

clue.text: Ridiculous muddle I leave — it's absurd

indicators.note: muddling the word mixes its letters into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letter that leaves

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a ridiculous mess, calling it absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave' tells you the I goes: RIDICULOUS minus one I, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludicrous means laughably foolish, the same as absurd.

clue.text: Is Ben confused with the playwright?

indicators.note: confused letters are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A question whether a man called Ben is being mistaken for a dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik, the Norwegian author of A Doll's House, is a famous dramatist.

clue.text: Excellent anaesthetic for one or two, perhaps

parts.note: prime means of the best quality
a numbing agent is something that numbs, a number

explanation.surface: An excellent painkiller for one or two patients.
explanation.walkthrough: NUMBER is read as 'numb-er', a thing that numbs. One was once counted among such numbers; two still is.
explanation.definitionFit: Two is divisible only by itself and one, so it is an example of this kind of integer.
